sources.title: Segui-Simarro et al. (2004), Electron Tomographic Analysis of Somatic Cell Plate Formation
sources.supports: Opened publisher abstract: late-anaphase initiation, vesicle fusion, tubulo-vesicular network, peripheral expansion and parental-wall connection.

findings.location: lines 178-185 and 210-211; fusing vesicle modulo reset in the implicit membrane field
findings.evidence: At p=0.5 +/- 1e-7, a ray from the lumen center through actual membrane triangles along +x hits x=0.5029747486 then x=0.4079757333: 0.0949990153 retreat. At p=0.7 +/- 1e-7, it hits 1.7702560425 then 1.6752573252: 0.0949987173 retreat. Both equal almost the entire 0.095 vesicle radius. The t≈1 fused bulge is deleted by the modulus reset while the plate radius itself barely changes.
findings.whyWrong: A represented fusion region abruptly collapses inward on every cycle despite the lesson showing continuous outward membrane addition. This is a discontinuity of the real cell-plate surface, not merely an invisible particle respawn.
findings.fix: Complete vesicle absorption continuously before reuse, retaining or smoothly incorporating its membrane into the plate margin; make the end-of-cycle field agree with the start-of-next-cycle field without reducing membrane detail.
findings.verification: Probe actual triangle surfaces on both sides of every cycle boundary, at +x and additional delivery angles. With successively smaller delta-progress, the boundary displacement must converge to zero while closed-lumen, parent-junction and exact-seek regressions remain intact.

continuity.checked: Full update formula review; existing 26-state exact-seek regression; actual surface ray diagnostics around p=.5 and .7; bounded 18-update CPU sample.
findings: Node update-only sample median 17.05 ms and max 27.86 ms; a potential browser frame-budget concern requiring isolated measurement.
limits: CPU sample was collected while parallel reviewers were active and does not prove browser FPS, GPU cost or a performance regression.

sources.supports: Opened author university abstract supports polarized zygote development and an asymmetric first division.

findings.evidence: The sperm sphere remains a complete independently visible plasma-membrane shell until p=.72 while its nucleus is a child of that shell. At p=.7 every sampled shell vertex of the egg-target sperm is inside the egg ellipsoid (normalized ellipsoid Q range .102-.494), so the intact sperm cell is transported into the egg interior. Meanwhile the central-target paternal nucleus center is outside the central-cell ellipsoid (Q=1.547 at .7; Q=1.484 at .719999; Q>1 is outside). Its limiting center z=.2689 exceeds the central gamete's maximum front z=.21. Both assignment branches reproduce the same failure. Maternal gamete surfaces are complete transparent ellipsoids, not meshes with a fusion opening.
findings.whyWrong: The scene conflates plasma-membrane fusion with transport of a whole intact sperm cell to the maternal nucleus, and routes the central sperm nucleus outside the female gamete it supposedly fertilizes. Correct n/2n/3n labels and an exact identity count do not repair this spatial/causal error.
findings.fix: Place and scale maternal nuclei and sperm nuclear routes within the female gamete compartments; depict sperm membrane merger at a real gamete contact before continuing only the paternal nucleus toward the maternal nucleus. Preserve both interchangeable sperm assignments and visible nuclear identities.
findings.verification: For both assignments, check actual rendered contact/surface geometry at plasmogamy, retain one paternal nucleus per target, and verify its subsequent world coordinates remain within the intended female gamete up to karyogamy. No intact separately bounded sperm plasma membrane may persist around an intragametic migrating nucleus.

findings.evidence: At p=.719999 the egg-target carried paternal nucleus is at [-.22,-.92,.2689]; at .72 its replacement marker appears at [-.13,-.92,.49], a .238716-unit jump. The central-target nucleus jumps from [0,.65,.2689] to [0,.77,.43], .200881 units. Both branches have identical target-specific jumps, while the prior visible nucleus radius is only about .027.
findings.whyWrong: The identity handoff preserves the count but abruptly relocates the tracked paternal contribution by several nuclear radii at the exact fusion milestone, weakening the viewer's ability to follow nuclear fusion.
findings.fix: Make the post-fusion contribution start at the same world position/size as the arriving paternal nucleus, then move or mix continuously within the maternal nucleus if needed. Keep exclusive identity ownership without an unmatched spatial switch.
findings.verification: At .72 +/- shrinking epsilon, match the outgoing and incoming visible paternal contribution positions and visual extents for both assignments. Preserve exactly two total paternal contributions through the handoff and deterministic reverse seeks.

continuity.checked: All path/reveal, visibility and handoff formulas; 26-state exact seeking; both assignments and actual world-position probes around .72.

sources.title: Riquelme et al. (2014), The Neurospora crassa exocyst complex tethers Spitzenkorper vesicles to the apical plasma membrane during polarized growth
sources.supports: Opened institutional full text: stratified Spitzenkorper, apical tethering and exocytotic events; vesicle PM merger delivers membrane and extracellular contents.

findings.evidence: Every transported object is an explicit vesicle shell with paired membrane rims and three cargo bodies. Its scale remains [.073,.073,.073] and it stays visible through the entire t<1 apical approach. The apical membrane is an unchanged translated sphere patch; there is no fusion neck, opening, shell incorporation or cargo/synthase transfer. At wrap the full carrier reappears at the base. Example normal carrier 0 jumps 5.216738 units at p=2/3 with unchanged visibility/scale; the reduced branch's visible carrier 16 also resets at full scale. Deposits are independently born at predefined progress values.
findings.whyWrong: The narrated causal event is vesicle fusion supplying apical membrane/synthases and extracellular wall material. Here a detailed intact carrier reaches the apical membrane location and returns intact to the base without depicting transfer, so the central advertised membrane-fusion event is absent and visually reads as intact-carrier recycling.
findings.fix: Represent at least one traceable apical fusion event using prebuilt or fixed-buffer continuous membrane/neck geometry with material/cargo transfer, then recycle carriers only after their individual delivery is no longer visibly intact. Retain ongoing flow, both controls, wall detail and septal clearance.
findings.verification: Track an actual carrier through contact and delivery in both branches. Require a continuous membrane connection/transfer during the fusion interval and no intact carrier teleport between apex and base. Preserve extracellular wall location, stationary deposited cohorts, exact seeking and resource inventories.

findings.evidence: At t=.68 the incoming formula ends with y=.096*sin(i*1.7), z=.2*cos(i*2.1), while the outgoing formula starts y=0,z=.12. The carrier is continuously visible at scale .073. Across p +/- 1e-7, actual positions jump .080-.247406 units in the normal branch and .124660-.227606 for the two reduced-branch visible crossings. Example reduced carrier 12 at p=.222222 moves [.88,.095980,.199548] to [.88,0,.12].
findings.whyWrong: This is a discontinuity in the same visible carrier's trajectory at its arrival at the Spitzenkorper, not an intentional staged appearance or a hidden flow reset. The largest jump exceeds the carrier diameter.
findings.fix: Make incoming and outgoing paths meet in the same three-dimensional position, with an eased tangent/velocity change or brief cluster dwell. Keep the central-pore convergence and both control speeds.
findings.verification: At every .68 branch crossing in both controls, positions on either side must converge as epsilon decreases. Also inspect velocity continuity and retain the entire-vesicle septal clearance regression.

continuity.checked: All formula branches, both delivery values, every first visible .68 junction and wrap, existing 26-state exact seeks and full pore-clearance tests.
